scope: Relative and endogenous value function iteration for finite MDPs: the span seminorm and the Dobrushin bound; constant-shift invariance of the Bellman operator and of greedy policies (White), relative value iteration as value iteration up to a constant, the span contraction sp(Tv - Tw) <= beta alpha sp(v - w); strong convergence of relative values at rate beta alpha, the MacQueen-Porteus policy error bound, Bray's stopping rule and its finite termination; White's average-reward theorem (beta = 1, alpha < 1): convergence to a solution of the average-reward optimality equation, optimality and uniqueness of the gain; endogenous value iteration for exogenous/endogenous state splits (Bray): invariance to exogenous shifts, the endogenizing operator, the within-x span contraction at rate beta alpha_y with alpha_y bounded by the full Dobrushin bound, recovery of v* and optimal policies from the endogenous value, the policy error bound, and an example where relative VFI gives no speed-up but endogenous VFI is exact.
source: White (1963); Morton and Wecker (1977); MacQueen (1966); Porteus (1971); Puterman (2005); Bray (2019, Quantitative Economics); Bray (2019, Management Science).
